_what_this_is: MACHINE FIRST PASS on extraction quality, NOT a completed human audit. Six real postings were read and compared against what skills.py extracted. Recorded as data so a person can disagree and re-score with tools/score_extraction.py.
_conflict_of_interest: Claude wrote skills.py AND these verdicts, and shares the dictionary's blind spots: terms the dictionary never contained are exactly the terms an author of it is least likely to notice are absent. That is the same failure mode as measuring recall on synthetic data. Treat the missed-term list as a LOWER BOUND on what is missing.
_method: For each posting, list skills a competent reader would say the posting asks for that the extractor did NOT return (missed), and returned terms that are not actually a stated requirement (false_positive). 'uncertain_fp' means the term may appear in company boilerplate rather than in the requirements.

_patterns: RECALL: the dictionary misses a great deal of ordinary backend tooling - Hibernate/JPA, ArgoCD, Istio, Helm, Gradle, Maven, GitOps, Next.js, Crossplane. Nine distinct misses across six postings.
RECALL: spelled-out forms are missed where only the abbreviation is an alias ('test-driven development' vs 'tdd'), and bare 'API' is missed because only 'rest api' is listed.
RECALL: the deliberate refusal to match bare 'Go' costs a real hit. That was the right call to avoid false positives, but the cost should be stated rather than hidden.
CONSTRUCT VALIDITY: several matches come from company or product boilerplate rather than the requirements section. A mention is not a requirement, and counting them the same way inflates every share.
